req.title: Index shows post author name
req.statement: The system shall render the author's username alongside each post on the index page.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-032 requires that the author's username is rendered alongside each post on the index page (GET /). The blog.index view JOINs post with user and passes 'username' to the template. Tests must verify: (1) positive — known posts appear with correct author usernames in the HTML response; (2) negative — when no posts exist the page still returns 200 with no author names rendered; (3) boundary — the most-recently-created post (highest created timestamp) appears first with its correct author. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes, exact username strings, exact ordering, and both presence and absence of specific byte strings.

tests.name: test_index_shows_author_username_for_all_posts
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 20 posts and 5 users as specified
Posts are authored by users: Rahul (id=1), Anjali (id=2), Ishaan (id=3), James (id=5)
No user session is required to view the index
actions: Create Flask app with test config and temp database
Initialise database with schema and seed data
Send GET / with the test client
Inspect response body for author usernames
expected: Response body does NOT contain b'Diya' (no posts by Diya)
trace: R-FLASKR-032: index renders author username alongside each post
EP: valid partition — database has posts with multiple distinct authors
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_shows_author_username_for_all_posts():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'Anjali' in r.data
    assert b'Ishaan' in r.data
    assert b'James' in r.data
    assert b'Diya' not in r.data

tests.name: test_index_single_post_author_username_exact
preconditions: A fresh database with exactly one user and one post inserted manually
actions: Create app with fresh temp database
Insert exactly one user 'Rahul' and one post authored by that user
Send GET / and check the response
trace: R-FLASKR-032: single-post boundary — exactly one author username rendered
BVA: boundary value — minimum non-empty post list (1 post); catches mutations that skip rendering username
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash

fd4, path4 = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd4)
app4 = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path4})
with app4.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute("INSERT INTO user (id, username, password) VALUES (1, 'Rahul', ?)",
               (generate_password_hash('stone'),))
    db.execute("INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id) VALUES ('Solo post', 'Body text', 1)")
    db.commit()
client4 = app4.test_client()

def test_index_single_post_author_username_exact():
    r = client4.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    html = r.data
    assert b'Rahul' in html
    assert b'Solo post' in html
    assert b'Anjali' not in html
    assert b'James' not in html
